To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the taphonomic and taxonomic composition of fossil assemblages from lacustrine environments can be correlated with depositional environments.
1) lacustrine fish assemblages change with nearshore to offshore distance, and 2) lacustrine plant assemblages change in abundance, and in the taxa represented with nearshore to off-shore distance.

the fish assemblages of the Willwood Formation are biased toward shallow water, near-shore environments and that the fish assembalages are biased in favor of the preservation of large, robust, and hard-bodied taxa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the taphonomy of fish, insects, and plants in ancient lacustrine environments in western North America.
the reconstruction of ancient lacustrine environments using both auto- and allochthonus fossils.
the reconstruction of the paleoecology of ancient lake environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fossil record of Eocene lake environments in western North America is not a simple reflection of the living community, but rather is a complex reflection of a variety of factors, including the nature of the lake environment, the nature of the community, and the nature of the taphonomic process.
the fossil record is a record of life and not a record of death.
the reconstruction of ancient lake environments is best done using both allochthonous and autochthonous fossil evidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Eocene lake environments in western North America were characterized by a mosaic of near-shore and offshore environments, which were subject to seasonal variation.
the Eocene lacustrines of western North America were seasonally stratified, and that the stratification was a result of the interplay between tectonic and climatic processes.
autochthonous assemblages are not representative of ancient lake communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to sample a range of depositional environments to reconstruct ancient communities.
the taphonomic and ecological biases that affect fossil assemblages must be considered in the reconstruction of ancient communities.
the fossil record can provide a wealth of information about past lake environments if we sample appropriately and are aware of taphonomic biases.
